newsitem.title: USA: CRV adds two nominees to Sallie Mae board.
newsitem.headline: CRV adds two nominees to Sallie Mae board.

text.p: The Committee to Restore Value at Sallie Mae said Thursday it had nominated two new people to the 15 nominees it has picked for the Sallie Mae board.
The CRV, one of two shareholder groups seeking to control Sallie Mae after it is privatized, said its new nominees are Diane Suitt Gilleland and Barry Munitz.
Gilleland serves on the current Sallie Mae board as a presidential appointee and also has served as vice chair of the board and on its Executive Committee.
Munitz is Chancellor and chief executive of the California State University System, the nation's largest senior system of higher education.
CRV spokesman Paul Carey said Gilleland and Munitz are the final nominees to the 15-member board that will serve the privatized company.
Sallie Mae (Student Loan Marketing Association) is a stockholder-owned U.S. government-sponsored company.
Sallie Mae and the CRV have been dueling since January, with both sides in favor of ending the organization's ties to the government but each disagreeing on business strategy.
Carey said an election for new board of the privatized company should come in about a month.
